newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht steady late, interbank rate higher.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht steady late, interbank rate higher.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate rose sharply late on Tuesday on higher baht demand used for buying dollar and possible intervention by the central bank to keep rates high, dealers said.

The baht weakened slightly late onshore to 32.65/32.75 per dollar, near its record low and against 32.60/32.70 in the morning. The dollar remained well bid, they said. It firmed to 32.680/32.780 offshore late, recovering from a record traded low of 32.90 earlier.
A central bank announcement that it may lift the two-tier system at an appropriate time failed to move the market.

"Dollar buying seemed to subside a bit in the afternoon," said a local dealer. "Buying was active in the past few days. Some attributed it to political concerns, but it could also be due to three-month forward contracts," she said.
The overnight interbank rate was quoted between 15 and 18 percent late on Tuesday against 15 percent earlier.
"The central bank may have absorbed liquidity to keep rates high," said a dealer from Thai Farmers Bank.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was steady at 19/24 satangs/dollar late onshore and eased slightly offshore to 35/45 against 38/45 in the morning.
